subject.title: [Feature]: Memory/Context Improvements (metrics + global semantic search + conversation chaining + preload on restart)

question: Should OpenClaw standardize privacy-scoped cross-session memory and restart preload as core behavior, and if so which parts belong in the first supported product contract?
rationale: The remaining request changes what private session material is indexed and inherited, adds operator/API surface, and may alter startup cost and existing user expectations; source-level implementation alone cannot choose those defaults.

options.title: Split and sequence the core contract
options.body: Keep this umbrella and create bounded follow-ups for session-memory policy, metrics API, and startup preload, with session privacy/defaults decided first.

options.title: Graduate session memory only
options.body: Prioritize a narrowly scoped, opt-in or privacy-scoped continuity feature and defer metrics and restart preload until their own contracts are designed.

options.title: Keep it extension-led
options.body: Document existing hooks and plugin/MCP seams while declining a new core default until a maintainer sponsors a concrete core contract.

recommendation.title: Split and sequence the core contract
recommendation.body: Keep this umbrella and create bounded follow-ups for session-memory policy, metrics API, and startup preload, with session privacy/defaults decided first.

likelyOwner.reason: The available feature-history evidence places steipete across the central memory, usage, and startup surfaces.
